gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-gowun-batang: Round forms like open parentheses, with no swell on any downstroke: that is Oldtimer. Gowun Batang sets against it with refined, literary serifs whose terminals pull back to leave wide gaps, a soft, bookish counterweight to such a commanding display face.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-habibi: Oldtimer draws its strokes like a fixed pen, round and commanding, with no calligraphic swell anywhere. And Habibi, a traditional serif with a clear channel before its round letters, gives the page an editorial, lower-key voice beneath it.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-labrada: Wirelike strokes of one thickness, bent into round forms like open parentheses, mark Oldtimer out. Labrada, a dignified text serif with wide openings on small letters, is the one built to carry the reading, while the heading simply announces.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-laila: Oldtimer keeps its round, parenthesis-like forms free of any calligraphic shading. Laila follows in an editorial, traditional serif voice, leaving generous space between curve ends and stems, so the commanding heading has a gentler partner below.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-rhodium-libre: Tube-like, constant-width strokes shaped into round forms like open parentheses give Oldtimer its commanding, classic look. Rhodium Libre handles the rest with lifted brush ends.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-rokkitt: Oldtimer is all wire-like monoline, round and commanding. Rokkitt, bookish and traditional, offers a c as open as a bent paperclip, so the pair gets its strongest effect from a hard-edged heading sitting over a softer, friendlier body.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-sanchez: Sanchez brings a bookish, dignified serif with calipers-wide c shapes. Oldtimer, drawn with pencil-line consistency in round, commanding forms, does its finest work as a big, short heading above it.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-solway: Authoritative from the first line, Oldtimer draws round forms like open parentheses without any calligraphic swell on its downstrokes. Solway, bookish and stencil-flat in weight, with a generous entry into the e, takes over the reading.
gen-dafont-origami-fs-amulya: Origami looks like one brush stroke, held at constant width. Amulya, a plain sans with generous gaps in its curves and a moderate lowercase, steps back so the heavy, lead-type mass of the heading stands out.
gen-dafont-origami-fs-plein: Unique is the first word for Origami, a single-stroke brush look with a lowercase mass like poured lead type. And Plein, a reliable, clean body face with a moderate lowercase, can sit at a modest size under a much larger heading.
